issues.legal_issue: A court cannot award equitable interest in addition to the interest and other amounts prescribed by the land acquisition statute.
material_facts: Possession of the land was taken before publication of the acquisition notification, and the Collector made the award after the notification.
The High Court directed payment of 12% interest on equitable grounds from the taking of possession until deposit, in addition to statutory interest and the additional amount under Section 23(1-A).
The award included the additional amount under Section 23(1-A) for the period from possession to the award.
issues.conclusion: The direction to award 12% equitable interest in addition to the statutory benefits was illegal and was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 31 and 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, interest is payable in the manner and at the rates prescribed by the statute. Where the statute governs interest, a court cannot award additional interest on equitable grounds. The Court relied on Mir Fazeelath Hussain v. Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition, Hyderabad, which held that equity does not determine the rate of interest where the statute prescribes it, and noted Kalimpong Land & Building Ltd. v. State of West Bengal in discussing equitable interest where a statute makes no specific provision.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation in a land acquisition matter.
predicates.statutory_interest_scheme_applies: The governing statute prescribes how interest is payable to the claimant.
predicates.additional_equitable_interest_awarded: A court awards interest on equitable grounds in addition to the statutory interest or other statutory amounts.

issues.definition: If a land acquisition compensation appeal concerns a statutory interest scheme and a court has awarded additional equitable interest, that additional interest is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory additional amount may be calculated from the taking of possession until the award when the possession is treated as referable to the acquisition notification.
material_facts: Possession of the land was taken before the acquisition notification was published.
The claimant did not challenge the validity of the acquisition notification.
The award calculated the additional amount under Section 23(1-A) from the date possession was taken until the award was made.
issues.conclusion: The direction to pay the additional amount under Section 23(1-A) from the taking of possession until the award was valid and was not disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1-A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 provides for an additional amount calculated over the relevant period. Because the claimant did not challenge the validity of the notification, the possession taken was to be treated as referable to that notification, supporting calculation from possession until the award.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and possession_precedes_notification and notification_validity_not_challenged and possession_referable_to_notification

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation in a land acquisition matter.
predicates.possession_precedes_notification: Possession of the acquired land was taken before publication of the acquisition notification.
predicates.notification_validity_not_challenged: The claimant did not challenge the validity of the acquisition notification.
predicates.possession_referable_to_notification: The possession taken is treated as referable to the acquisition notification.

issues.definition: When possession precedes the notification but its validity is not challenged and the possession is treated as referable to that notification, the additional amount may run from possession until the award.
